title: Attempt to suicide - decriminalised but still misunderstood
p1:
A person survives a suicide attempt… and many still ask, “Will they be punished?”

The answer surprises many people: the law moved away from punishment, but society has not fully moved away from judgment.
p2:
Attempt to suicide was decriminalised in India through the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017. This means a person who attempts suicide is presumed to be under severe stress and should receive care and support, not punishment.

The lesser-known part? The focus shifted from treating the act as a crime to recognising the mental and emotional suffering behind it.
p3:
This change reminds us that a suicide attempt is often a sign of a crisis, not a character flaw. The right response is empathy, professional help, and support systems that address the reasons behind the distress.

A legal change can remove punishment, but changing social attitudes takes more time.
conclusion: Do you think society has truly understood the purpose behind decriminalising attempt to suicide, or do stigma and misconceptions still remain?
